title: Water Damage Mitigation Compliance Bulletin: Disposal of Removed Baseboard
content:
**Compliance bulletin — baseboard trim on Water Damage Mitigation tear-out**

Trim disposal depends on the building and the water, measured on the baseboard run, the total linear feet on the job's baseboard removal lines. It sets the trim loads that the job's tear-out debris haul-off line carries:
- in a building built before the RRP year-built cutoff of the job's tier, the baseboard is bagged as lead-painted trim and hauled as its own loads, so the trim loads are the baseboard run divided by 150 linear feet per load, rounded up to a whole load on its own;
- in a building built in or after that cutoff year on a Category 3 job, the contaminated baseboard is discarded with the drywall, so the trim loads are the baseboard run divided by 120 linear feet per load, not rounded on its own but added unrounded to the drywall and flooring loads;
- in any other case no trim disposal arises, the baseboard being detached for reset.

The RRP year-built cutoff is 1978 on every Water Damage Mitigation tier (Clean, Gray and Black Water Mitigation, Standard Loss and Large Loss alike). The year built and the IICRC water category are those recorded on the job.

## Truth table (hypothetical buildings)
| Year built | Water category | Trim loads |
|---|---|---|
| 1965 | any | baseboard run divided by 150, rounded up on its own |
| 1977 | Category 3 | baseboard run divided by 150, rounded up on its own |
| 1978 | Category 3 | baseboard run divided by 120, unrounded |
| 1995 | Category 3 | baseboard run divided by 120, unrounded |
| 1978 or later | Category 1 or 2 | none |

## Worked figures (hypothetical run of 200 linear feet)
- Built 1965: 200 divided by 150 is 1.33, rounded up on its own to 2 trim loads.
- Built 1995, Category 3: 200 divided by 120 is 1.67, carried unrounded into the job's loads.
